newsitem.title: RUSSIA: No extra troops in southern Russia - Kulikov.
newsitem.headline: No extra troops in southern Russia - Kulikov.

text.p: Russia will not send additional forces to volatile southern regions bordering rebel Chechnya despite a spate of violence, Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov said on Wednesday .

"There are no plans to build up troops in the area," Russian Public Television showed Kulikov telling reporters after meeting President Boris Yeltsin at the Black Sea resort of Sochi where the Kremlin leader is on vacation.
The situation around Chechnya, where 21 months of war between Moscow troops and rebels ended in a shaky truce last August, has deteriorated sharply over the past week.
On Wednesday a senior official in the ethnic region of Ingushetia, which neighbours Chechnya, was killed by unidentified gunmen.
Russian police clashed early on Tuesday outside Chechnya with what Kulikov said was a group of 20 rebel fighters.

A day earlier two people were killed and more that 20 wounded in an explosion at the railway station in the southern Russian spa resort of Pyatigorsk. Last Wednesday two people were killed in a similar blast in the southern town of Armavir.
Russian news agencies have quoted security officials as saying that in most cases they could trace a Chechen connection.
Kulikov has said that two Chechen women fighters, seized after the Pyatigorsk blast, have admitted planting an explosive device.

Chechen officials have denied responsibility for any of the violent acts and accused Russian security services of staging a provocation to disrupt peace talks aimed at reaching a long-term peace deal between Russia and Chechnya.
Kulikov said police had stepped up security in the area to prevent the infiltration of guerrilla groups from Chechnya.

Despited the renewed war of words, Russian officials appeared reluctant to put at risk the peace talks. Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Tuesday they would continue despite the latest incidents.
